title: Brand Kit commands claim completion without performing the named action
impact: A Filmmaker can believe versions were opened, assets reordered, moved or made primary when only a transient success toast changes. This undermines the production reference and obscures unfinished workflows.
observed: Manage versions only invokes notify("Version management opened"); Reorder only says ready to reorder; Set as primary only reports success; Move to sub-brand clears selection after a toast without changing a brand. Many per-file/bulk Download commands report download started without producing a file. Actual editor-files download-all is a separate data anchor, so commands are not interchangeable.
expected: A labelled command opens its workflow or produces its advertised result. Front-end-only scope permits local simulations, but their outcome must be honest and reviewable.
authority: User audit section 9: controls that appear usable but do nothing, feedback and recovery
AGENTS.md: front-end reference mission and requested happy path
recommendation: Finish a small coherent local mock interaction for each intended command, or mark the command as an unavailable prototype step with explanatory copy. Remove false success feedback. Prioritise Manage versions, Set as primary and Move to sub-brand; keep actual downloads separate from simulated actions.
rationale: This corrects the action/result contract without adding a backend or inventing a download service.
alternatives: Hide unfinished commands if they are outside the approved scope; alternatively retain discoverability with a clear disabled explanation.
tradeoffs: Hiding loses review visibility; disabled controls require concise explanations. Do not turn a mock notification into a real integration.
rootCause: Command callbacks use notification-only stubs alongside functional commands with identical presentation.
occurrences: Motion: Download video and Manage versions
Tile menus: Download all and Reorder
Selected assets: Download and Move to sub-brand
Editor file menu: Copy link reports copied via onDownload

title: Guest logo preview exposes Replace and Delete
impact: A recipient of a shared Brand Kit encounters editing and destructive controls in an intended read-only preview. Even transient changes misrepresent who can manage the Studio assets.
observed: LogoVariant is clickable regardless of canEdit. LogoDownloadModal always receives Replace/Delete callbacks and renders those actions without a canEdit prop. isGuest prevents BrandKitContext persistence but updateSection still changes local profile state. Thus this is an exposed read-only affordance and transient mutation risk, not evidence of persistent guest writes.
expected: Guest/read-only asset previews permit reading/downloading and omit management commands. Capability checks should govern both action display and handlers.
authority: brisk-saas-patterns.md: every feature answers who can see and act
User audit section 4: read-only and restricted states
recommendation: Pass the existing edit capability into the logo preview; show Replace/Delete only when permitted and guard callbacks. Preserve genuine download choices for recipients.
rationale: Use the capability already established for the surrounding asset tile instead of creating a new role model.
alternatives: Separate a guest download-only dialog from the editable dialog only if the content differs materially.
tradeoffs: A split dialog risks duplication; one capability-aware dialog is smaller. Existing Client-editable Brand Kits must retain their approved management capabilities.
rootCause: The tile gates AssetActions, but the nested logo dialog does not inherit that gate.
occurrences: All logo cards opened from guest shared kits

title: Client project navigation silently changes the viewer to another Client
impact: If confirmed, a Client viewing Loom may open another Client project or portal by URL because route context selects that Client and a permitted contact before access checks. The prototype could teach the wrong isolation behaviour.
observed: Lead verified Customer Jess Taylor on the Loom portal (E014), then directly opened /projects/deel-customer-story/stages/brief without a role/scenario change. Deel Brief opened under Priya Nair while the account subtitle still said Loom (E015). Source root: URL project lookup provides contextualProject.clientId ahead of scenario/session client, then invited projectMember is selected ahead of the original participant. ProjectAccessGate validates that substituted contact rather than the original Jess identity.
expected: Customer membership and Client identity remain anchored to the selected viewer; Studio Staff alone can preview any Client without changing identity. Test mode changes should be explicit and separate from navigation.
authority: AGENTS.md: one dataset with visibility per role, Customer access scoped to memberships
brisk-saas-patterns.md: Clients never see another Client projects; Staff preview keeps identity

tradeoffs: Fixing context selection may reveal previously convenient demo links as unavailable. Validate scenario entry and export URLs, then choose coherent fallback copy.

title: Script and Storyboard version authoring does not inherit project edit capability
impact: A Client or a Freelancer assigned to a different stage may receive Create, Duplicate and Rename commands that alter current versions and can restart an approved stage. The expected boundary between viewing, reviewing and authoring is unclear.
observed: Both pages always supply create/duplicate/rename callbacks to ScriptVersionControl. Script createNewScriptDocument and duplicateVersion do not check canActOnProject; guardEditable protects approved row changes only. Storyboard context mutations also do not check the viewer. Script/Storyboard version arrays are displayed in full; a release-to-Client model is not present in their version records. Shared ProjectAccessGate checks viewing only.
expected: The existing project capability model makes Customer edit=false for non-Media stages and limits Freelancer editing to assigned stages. Production guidance requires Clients to see released versions only. Any deliberate co-authoring exception needs an explicit scoped decision.
authority: AGENTS.md: preserve role and workflow boundaries
recommendation: Resolve Client co-authoring/release intent with Tom before implementation. At minimum align version-management command visibility and handlers with approved edit capability while preserving review/approval and historical viewing. Define which versions Clients may view if the release rule applies to these document stages.
rationale: Selecting a historical version, making a new authoring version and approving work are distinct actions and should not share an accidental broad permission.
alternatives: Explicitly approve Client co-authoring for selected stages, with separate authored/released states, rather than applying blanket read-only to all Client document interactions.
tradeoffs: Broadly hiding version controls could remove useful history and approved review behaviour. Do not conflate Author permission with Approve permission or change stored role identifiers.
rootCause: Version control composes authoring callbacks independently from project capability model; version data lacks release scope.

title: Client settings default to an Admin preview independently of the current contact
impact: Client account settings can show company/team management to a contact without deriving the contact membership. Restricted states are selected by a hidden URL parameter, which may mislead demonstrations of the approved three access roles.
observed: ClientAccountSettingsContext sets access.role to Client Admin unless client-role=member is present. It does not derive this from usePrototypeViewer or the current contact. Company/team data derive from state.session.activeClientId while project/portal viewer context can derive from route. ClientInvoices retains shared stored account invoices while replacing only company/team metadata for another active Client. These are source-supported context mismatches; current available fixture may have only Loom records.
expected: Three access roles remain the prototype authority; any approved within-Client responsibility should derive from the explicit current viewer/contact and Client, or be clearly labelled as an isolated preview. Client finances must remain scoped.
authority: AGENTS.md: exactly three access roles; no additional granular permission screens unless explicitly requested
brisk-saas-patterns.md: settings scopes separate and Client data isolated
recommendation: Ask Tom to confirm whether Client Admin/Member is an intentional retained demonstration. Derive rendered capability/company/invoices from the same scoped viewer when live; move URL-driven variants into clearly labelled preview context if retained. Do not add a new permission system.
rationale: Clarifies what the prototype proves about access and prevents current URL/defaults being treated as approved product behaviour.
alternatives: Keep legacy account settings as explicitly excluded demonstration pages until a later scoped Client settings ticket, rather than expanding the current audit into implementation.
tradeoffs: Removing tiers without approval could erase intentional responsibility distinctions. A source-driven fix needs existing contact data and finance scoping verified before changing UI.
rootCause: Legacy settings preview access uses query parameters and global stored account data separately from canonical viewer state.

title: Direct Storyboard creation falls back to the global Harbour Health Script
impact: Creating a Storyboard from the project stage can populate a different Client narrative, while conversion from the project Script uses the actual selected approved version. Users cannot trust what the Create confirmation refers to.
confidence: High for divergent source paths; current stored Loom board provenance uncertain
observed: Lead saw a persisted Loom Storyboard containing Harbour Health/Maya content. Initial Storyboard records seed only Notion, so the existing Loom board cannot be attributed to the current default seed alone. Source independently confirms that the direct Create confirmation omits sourceVersion, and createStoryboardRecord defaults to getLatestApprovedScriptVersion from the global Harbour Health script fixtures. The Script-page conversion passes its selectedVersion rows explicitly. No create action was performed during this audit.
expected: Create Storyboard from the approved Script means the approved Script of the same project. Both creation entry points should resolve identical project-scoped source data.
authority: brisk-production-journey.md: Script and Storyboard are project artefacts; Client data isolation

AGENTS.md: one dataset shared across views and project-specific workflows
recommendation: Resolve the approved Script for the target project once and pass it explicitly in both creation paths. If no approved project Script is available, show the existing prerequisite state rather than silently using a global sample.
